ai.literal: Wife they-who-desire excellent benefit they-attain-not; action they-who-desire rejecting thing-also that.
ai.translation: Those who lust after their wives will not attain excellent benefits; that is also a thing rejected by those who desire great action.
ai.modern: மனைவியின் மீது அதீத ஆசை கொண்டவர்கள் சிறந்த பயன்களை அடைய மாட்டார்கள். செயலில் வெற்றி பெற விரும்புபவர்கள் வெறுத்து ஒதுக்கும் பொருளும் அந்த பெண்ணாசையே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against letting infatuation with one's wife override one's duties. The word 'maṉai' (household) here stands metonymically for the wife, and 'viḻaivār' refers to those who excessively desire or lust after her. Such people cannot achieve 'māṇ payaṉ' (excellent benefits or glorious results) in life. Furthermore, the text notes that this kind of infatuation ('atu') is exactly the thing rejected ('vēṇṭā poruḷ') by those who are committed to meaningful action ('viṉai viḻaiyār').

ai.literal: Disregarding, woman he-who-desires' wealth, great a shame to-become, shame will-give.
ai.translation: The wealth of a man who disregards his duty and blindly desires his wife will only bring him shame, becoming a great disgrace.
ai.modern: தன் கடமையைப் போற்றாமல் மனைவியின் விருப்பத்தையே விரும்பி வாழ்பவனின் செல்வம், அவனுக்குப் பெரியதொரு அவமானமாக மாறி வெட்கத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against a man becoming overly infatuated with his wife at the expense of his own duties. The word 'பேணாது' (disregarding) implies neglecting one's responsibilities or honor. 'பெண் விழைவான்' refers to a man who is entirely driven by his desire for his woman. The couplet states that any 'ஆக்கம்' (wealth or success) such a man possesses is useless; instead of bringing him respect, it will only result in profound shame.

ai.literal: With wife subordinated nature's lack always among good people shame will give.
ai.translation: The unnatural state of being subordinated to one's wife will always bring shame among good people.
ai.modern: மனைவியிடம் தாழ்ந்து நடக்கும் இயல்பற்ற நிலை ஒருவனுக்கு நல்லவர்களிடையே எப்போதும் வெட்கத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns about the social consequences of a man being overly submissive to his wife. The phrase இல்லாள்கண் தாழ்ந்த describes the act of being subordinated to one's spouse. The word இன்மை means absence or lack, and here combined with இயல்பு (nature) it means a lack of proper nature or unnatural conduct. The word நல்லார் can sometimes mean women, but here it takes the sense of good and wise people. Because of his undignified behavior, such a man will always face shame when among the good.

ai.literal: Wife (acc.) who fears, next-world man-without, action capability greatness attaining is-not.
ai.translation: The man who fears his wife lacks the rewards of the next world, and his capability in action will never attain greatness.
ai.modern: தன் மனைவிக்கு அஞ்சுகின்ற, மறுமைப் பயன் இல்லாதவனுடைய செயல் திறம் எந்தப் பெருமையையும் அடையாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the consequences of a man fearing his wife. The phrase 'மறுமை இலாளன்' (man without a next world) implies that by yielding to fear, he fails to perform righteous duties that secure future rewards. Consequently, his 'வினை ஆண்மை' (manliness or capability in action) becomes fruitless. Even if he undertakes great tasks, his efforts will lack 'வீறு' (splendor or greatness) because his fundamental lack of courage undermines his achievements.

ai.literal: Wife (acc.) he who fears, will fear indeed always, to good people good things to do.
ai.translation: He who fears his wife will always be afraid to do good deeds for good people.
ai.modern: தன் மனைவிக்கு அஞ்சுகின்றவன், நல்லவர்களுக்கு நல்ல செயல்களைச் செய்வதற்கும் எப்போதும் அஞ்சுவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that a man who is overly afraid of his wife will lack the courage to perform virtuous deeds. 'இல்லாளை அஞ்சுவான்' refers to a husband who lives in constant fear of his wife's displeasure. Because his actions are entirely dictated by this fear, he 'அஞ்சும்' (will fear) to do 'நல்ல' (good things) for 'நல்லார்க்கு' (good people) at all times ('எஞ்ஞான்றும்'). Thus, his submissiveness prevents him from fulfilling his moral and social duties.

ai.literal: Like the gods even if they live, greatness they are without indeed, wife's bamboo resembling shoulders those who fear.
ai.translation: Even if they live a life like that of the gods, men who fear their wife's bamboo-like shoulders have no true greatness.
ai.modern: தம் மனைவியின் மூங்கில் போன்ற தோள்களைக் கண்டு அஞ்சுகின்ற கணவர்கள், தேவர்களைப் போலச் சிறந்த வாழ்க்கை வாழ்ந்தாலும் எந்தப் பெருமையும் இல்லாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet criticizes men who are overly submissive to their wives out of fear. The phrase 'அமையார்தோள்' (bamboo-like shoulders) is a classical metaphor for a woman's beautiful, smooth shoulders, highlighting the irony of fearing something so delicate. 'இமையார்' refers to the gods, who are traditionally believed not to blink. The poet states that even if such men achieve a heavenly, god-like status in life, their cowardly submission strips them of all true dignity and greatness ('பாடு').

ai.literal: Woman's command having done behaving than the manliness, modesty possessing woman indeed greatness possesses.
ai.translation: A modest woman possesses more greatness than the manliness of a man who conducts himself by doing a woman's bidding.
ai.modern: பெண்ணின் கட்டளையைச் செய்து வாழும் ஆணின் ஆண்மையை விட, நாணம் கொண்ட பெண்ணே அதிக பெருமை உடையவள் ஆவாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts a submissive man with a modest woman to emphasize the loss of dignity in being uxorious. The phrase 'peṇ ēval ceytu oḻukum' describes a man who lives by executing a woman's commands. The poet states that a woman possessing natural modesty ('nāṇ uṭai peṇ') has far more greatness than the so-called 'manliness' ('āṇmaiyiṉ') of such a man. The emphatic 'ē' in 'peṇṇē' stresses that the woman herself is superior in stature to the man who blindly obeys her.

ai.literal: Friends' needs they will not fulfill; good they will not do; the good-foreheaded woman's desires as they follow.
ai.translation: Those who conduct themselves exactly as their beautiful wives desire will neither fulfill the needs of their friends nor do any good deeds.
ai.modern: தம் மனைவியின் விருப்பப்படி மட்டுமே நடப்பவர்கள், தம் நண்பர்களின் குறைகளைத் தீர்க்க மாட்டார்கள்; எந்த ஒரு நற்செயலையும் செய்ய மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against blindly following a wife's dictates. The phrase 'நன்னுதலாள் பெட்டாங்கு ஒழுகுபவர்' refers to men who act only according to the desires of their beautiful wives. Because their focus is entirely consumed by her wishes, they neglect their broader social duties. Consequently, they fail to help their friends in times of need and are unable to perform virtuous deeds for the wider community.

ai.literal: Virtuous deeds and, excellent wealth and, other deeds and, woman's command those who do-with, are not.
ai.translation: Virtuous deeds, abundant wealth, and other achievements are not found with those who do a woman's bidding.
ai.modern: பெண்ணின் கட்டளைக்குக் கீழ்ப்படிந்து நடப்பவர்களிடம் அறச்செயல்களும், சிறந்த செல்வமும், பிற நல்ல செயல்களும் இருக்கமாட்டா.
ai.explanation: This couplet states that men who blindly follow a woman's commands will fail to achieve anything of value. The word 'பொருள்' can mean meaning or wealth, but here it means wealth or material success, fitting alongside virtue and other deeds. The word 'கண்' acts as a locative suffix meaning 'with' or 'in the place of'. By using 'இல்' (do not exist), the verse emphasizes that subservience completely deprives a man of moral, material, and practical accomplishments.

ai.literal: Thought joined heart-in strength to those who possess, always woman joined-becoming folly is not.
ai.translation: Those who possess a strong mind filled with deep thought will never suffer the folly that comes from being subservient to a woman.
ai.modern: சிறந்த எண்ணங்கள் நிறைந்த நெஞ்சத்தின் வலிமை உடையவர்களுக்கு, எந்தக் காலத்திலும் மனைவியின் விருப்பத்திற்கு வளைந்து கொடுப்பதால் வரும் அறியாமை இருக்காது.
ai.explanation: The word 'எண்' refers to deep thought or wisdom, and 'இடன்' refers to the spaciousness or strength of the mind. The couplet states that men who possess a strong, thoughtful mind will not fall into the foolishness of blindly following a woman's dictates. Their inner strength and clarity of thought protect them from such weakness at all times. The phrase 'பெண் சேர்ந்தாம் பேதைமை' specifically points to the folly that arises from inappropriate subservience to a wife.
